about.title: Marina Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Marina's collision numbers tell a quiet but real story: 66 injury collisions and 88 people hurt in the most recent final reporting year, with one traffic death. Much of the reported activity clusters on corridors like Reservation Road, Imjin Parkway, and Del Monte Boulevard, and Wednesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. see more reports than other times. Behind each of those numbers is someone dealing with pain, missed work, and insurance calls they didn't ask for. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects people hurt in Monterey County crashes with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain options. There's no obligation to move forward, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is made. If a Marina crash has upended your week, it costs nothing to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or public agency — was involved. An attorney can flag that early so a claim doesn't get lost to a missed deadline.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Wording Matters
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible, you can still recover a share of damages. What you say in a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to shift blame onto you, which is why declining that call until you've spoken with an attorney is worth considering.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and attorneys connected through LawProactive work on contingency — no fee unless there's a recovery. That structure means getting advice costs nothing while evidence is still fresh.

items.question: Do I need to give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're not required to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can work against you. Insurers sometimes use those statements to argue you were more at fault under California's comparative fault rules. It's generally safer to talk to an independent attorney first.

items.question: What if my crash happened near Imjin Parkway or another busy Marina road?
items.answer: Corridors like Imjin Parkway, Reservation Road, and Del Monte Boulevard see a higher volume of reported collisions in Marina, which can mean more available evidence like traffic cameras, prior reports, or witnesses nearby. An attorney can help determine what evidence to gather quickly before it disappears. Every case still depends on its own specific facts.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Marina car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That deadline can be much shorter — sometimes six months — if a government entity, like a public road authority, may be responsible. Because these timelines vary, it helps to talk to an attorney sooner rather than later.
